open_questions.issue: FAO small-scale aquaponic food production manual provenance and completeness review remains open
open_questions.why_unresolved: FAO-derived atomic facts now exist locally, but the remaining issue is verifying provenance coverage and completeness against the intended primary-text sections.
open_questions.evidence_still_needed: Review mapped FAO-derived atomic facts against the manual sections needed for pH, filtration, pumps/aeration, and monitoring targets.

open_questions.issue: Pump power draw anchor contradiction: 0.37 kW vs 0.74 kW at similar reported flow
open_questions.why_unresolved: Same UVI hosted-copy document reports different motor ratings across system versions or trials.
open_questions.evidence_still_needed: Identify which value corresponds to which UVI system configuration and whether it is nameplate or measured draw.

open_questions.issue: TAN-from-feed alternative rule 2.2 lb NH3-N per 100 lb feed not reconciled with the protein-based equation
open_questions.why_unresolved: Reports flag it as provisional pending reconciliation of assumptions such as protein percent, assimilation, and solids removal.
open_questions.evidence_still_needed: Decide a single canonical TAN production model, with the protein-based model preferred and the alternative retained only as a cross-check.

open_questions.issue: Lettuce preferred pH 6.0-7.0 in some small-system tables vs tight CEA optimum near 5.8
open_questions.why_unresolved: Lettuce report flags the 6-7 table values as context-dependent and potentially not trial-derived.
open_questions.evidence_still_needed: Decide whether to add a small-system or low-precision mode, or keep one global lettuce pH optimum.

open_questions.issue: Basil tolerates pH as low as 4.0 in a short trial vs toxicity guidance below 5.8 in soilless substrate
open_questions.why_unresolved: Basil report flags likely differences by system type, nutrient recipe, and duration.
open_questions.evidence_still_needed: Decide whether to encode pH below 5.8 as disorder risk and reserve pH 4.0 for special-case experiments only.

open_questions.issue: Missing direct energy-per-oxygenation anchors such as kg O2/kWh or blower curves in uploaded reports
open_questions.why_unresolved: Pump and aeration report provides only limited kW anchors from UVI; not enough for general energy modelling.
open_questions.evidence_still_needed: Tier 1-2 RAS or aquaponics engineering manuals, or peer-reviewed aeration efficiency studies, to parameterize energy models.

open_questions.issue: DWC depth anchors vary across contexts: 10-12 inches, 15-30 cm, and UVI 12-inch raft water depth
open_questions.why_unresolved: The corroboration reports support multiple depth anchors from different contexts rather than one universal DWC depth default.
open_questions.evidence_still_needed: Keep depth anchors split by small-scale, hydroponic baseline, and UVI-style commercial contexts unless a stronger unifying rule emerges.

open_questions.issue: NFT biofilter requirement remains context-split between conditional wording and effectively required separate biofilter practice
open_questions.why_unresolved: Reports support low built-in nitrification in NFT and frequent separate-biofilter use, but not a single unconditional rule for every context.
open_questions.evidence_still_needed: Retain context-split handling unless a stronger architecture-specific sizing rule justifies a universal NFT biofilter requirement.

open_questions.issue: Solids management remains split between high-efficiency removal and lower-removal mineralisation strategies
open_questions.why_unresolved: Both strategies are supported, but under different loading and management contexts rather than as one universal default.
open_questions.evidence_still_needed: Preserve strategy split and tie default selection to system loading, maintenance burden, and architecture context.

open_questions.issue: Lettuce downy mildew uses both a 5-7 hour epidemiology window and an about-3-hour fast-infection context
open_questions.why_unresolved: The greenhouse corroboration report explicitly supports both windows in different disease-context framings.
open_questions.evidence_still_needed: Keep the fast-infection rule and the longer epidemiology window separate in models and controls rather than flattening them into one threshold.

open_questions.issue: Species-profile compatibility cleanup is needed to separate runtime-only alias handling from canonical knowledge-field requirements.
open_questions.why_unresolved: Current runtime sync preserves legacy alias behavior, while canonical knowledge files should remain authoritative on canonical names without manual alias duplication.
open_questions.evidence_still_needed: Confirm which alias pairs stay runtime-only compatibility output and which names, if any, have a canonical requirement in data/knowledge/species/**.

open_questions.issue: KEMA radish heat demand at the same 12/8 C setpoints: about 5.4 m3 a.e./m2/yr (KEMA 2009, edepot 289333) vs 12.0 m3 a.e./m2/yr (KEMA 2012, edepot 289335)
open_questions.why_unresolved: Both are KEMA reports for Kas als Energiebron with the same crop and setpoints; the reason for the 2x difference (house, screen, reference year, or heat vs gas basis) was not found in what was read.
open_questions.evidence_still_needed: Read both reports' method sections and compare house type, screen, reference year and whether the figure is heat demand or gas use. The heat demand model is calibrated on the 2012 figure; if 2009 is right, NL heat demand estimates roughly halve.

open_questions.issue: Tilapia growth is underpredicted at 23.5 to 25 C: Savidov 2005 fish harvest -38 percent at 24.8 C, Khater 2023 daily gain -20 to -36 percent at 23.5 C, model FCR 3.2 vs published 0.9 to 1.2; UVI reports only a slight winter depression at 24 C.
open_questions.why_unresolved: The temperature factor is linear between sourced points at 22 C (one third) and 27 C (full); the shape between them is assumed. No thermal growth coefficient for Nile tilapia was found.
open_questions.evidence_still_needed: A measured growth-vs-temperature curve for Nile tilapia (e.g. Azaza et al. 2008, juveniles in RAS at 22 to 34 C) to replace the straight line; then rerun scripts/validate_published_systems.py.
open_questions.resolution_note: 2026-11-26: temperature points replaced with Santos et al. 2013 measured rates (22 C 0.674) and Baras 2001 upper shoulder; Savidov fish -38 -> -25 percent, Khater gain -36 -> -10 percent. Khater FCR still +84 percent (published 0.92 to 1.20 is below the Tier 1 1.4 to 1.8 range). 2026-11-26 (round 3): Savidov fish is now scored against the report's own per-fish range 0.50 to 0.64 kg (model 471 g, -6 percent from the low end; -25 percent against the 630 g point, which assumes no mortality). The model still sits below the range, so slow growth at 24.8 C is not fully explained.

open_questions.issue: Basil per-plant growth is fixed from the UVI anchor (8 plants/m2), so yield per m2 scales with density: Savidov 2005 at 31.8 plants/m2 is overpredicted +286 percent (at UVI density the per-m2 yield is within 3 percent). Under low autumn light (Knaus 2018, PAR about 111 to 147 umol/m2/s) basil is overpredicted about 7x.
open_questions.why_unresolved: The plant model has no density or light response; it is calibrated to one site.
open_questions.evidence_still_needed: A basil yield response to planting density and to daily light integral from Tier 1 or 2 sources.
open_questions.resolution_note: 2026-11-26: density (Ciriello 2021 exponent) and DLI (Dou 2018, Walters 2023) factors added; Savidov +286 -> +68 percent; Knaus +670 -> +30 to +441 percent depending on the DLI reading (photoperiod not reported). 2026-11-26 (second fix): closed-canopy density rule (b = 0 above 8 plants/m2; Ciriello exponent kept as open-canopy sensitivity) and Knaus DLI re-derived from the paper as 4.3 to 7.2 (the 12.7 reading was ruled out by the paper's separate night PAR). Savidov +68 -> -2 percent; Knaus basil -13 percent at DLI 4.3, +112 percent at 7.2. The upper Knaus case still fails; see UQ-016.

open_questions.issue: In the Knaus 2018 tilapia unit (gravel beds, 20 g feed per m2 plant area per day, pH 8.0), modelled TAN is about 2x the published 0.21 mg/L and NO3-N about 32 percent below the published 15.6 mg/L.
open_questions.why_unresolved: Gravel media has more nitrifying surface than a raft but is counted as raft area; the residual N loss fraction is calibrated at UVI's feed ratio and solids handling only.
open_questions.evidence_still_needed: Nitrification capacity per m2 of gravel media bed; denitrification or solids N loss at low feed ratios.
open_questions.resolution_note: 2026-11-26: gravel beds now count as media volume x feed loading (new candidate variant media_bed_gravel_ebb_flow, 1.0 to 3.6 kg feed/m3/day from FAO 589 and SRAC 453, cross-checked with Greiner and Timmons 1998), not as raft area. Knaus beds: 2,000 kg of 16 to 32 mm gravel, about 1.25 to 1.43 m3 at a sand bulk-density proxy. At 3.6 kg/m3 TAN is 0.17 vs 0.21 mg/L (-20 percent) and NO3-N 17.8 vs 15.6 (+15 percent); at the FAO low end TAN is 0.65 (+210 percent). The observed TAN sits near the trickling-filter end, which the measured Greiner rates support. One validation point only.

open_questions.issue: Basil grown from three-week-old transplants is given the regrowth rate of UVI's established, cut-and-regrow plants from day 0. Knaus 2018 (70 days, low autumn light) is overpredicted +112 percent at the upper light estimate (DLI 7.2) and -13 percent at the lower (4.3).
open_questions.why_unresolved: No establishment lag or first-cut penalty is modelled; Knaus photoperiod and glasshouse air temperature are not reported, so light and temperature also remain uncertain.
open_questions.evidence_still_needed: Basil first-cut vs later-cut yields from transplant in raft or media beds (e.g. Modarelli 2023, Corrado 2020 full figures), and a basil temperature response for air below the water temperature.
open_questions.resolution_note: 2026-11-26 (round 3): the establishment-lag idea is not supported as a general rule. First cut vs regrowth cut, per day: UVI batch raft 2.1 vs 2.0, 1.7, 2.0 kg/m2 (no lag); Modarelli 2023 aquaponic raft 32.4 g in 35 d vs 44.4 g in 44 d (0.92 vs 1.01 g/d); Corrado 2020 first cut higher, second about 20 percent lower; only UVI staggered raft shows a lag (1.2 vs 2.4 kg/m2, authors: 'slow growth after transplanting while it became established'). No lag was added; UVI staggered is kept as evidence (truth BEV_0001). The real cause of the Knaus +112 percent was pH: the model let pH drift from the published 8.0 to about 7.5 by day 25, which doubled the basil score (see UQ-018). With pH held at 8.0, basil at the midpoint DLI is -24 percent (band -48 to +30 percent across the DLI bounds).

open_questions.issue: The model raises FCR as temperature falls (FCR = 1.7 / f_T, so 2.2 at 23.5 C). Khater 2023 prints FCR 0.92 to 1.20 at 23.5 C, below the Tier 1 range 1.4 to 1.8 and below UVI's 1.71 to 1.92.
open_questions.why_unresolved: The literature conflicts on direction: Workagegn 2014 (24 to 34 C) finds feed use worst at 24 C; Azaza 2008 (22 to 34 C) finds FCR best at 26 and 30 C; Mirea 2013 (20 to 30 C) finds FCR rising with temperature. Khater's FCR cannot be recomputed because feed intake is not printed, and its Eq. 5 mixes per-fish gain with the final fish count.
open_questions.evidence_still_needed: Measured FCR and feed intake by temperature for Nile tilapia above 30 g (Azaza 2008 and Mirea 2013 tables), to decide whether cool water lowers intake, conversion, or both. Until then the Khater FCR is reported but not scored.

open_questions.issue: simulate_day lowers pH by 0.01 per mg/L TAN nitrified with no alkalinity or water-hardness buffer, so an uncontrolled system drifts down steadily. In the Knaus run pH fell from the published mean of 8.0 to about 7.5 within 25 days and the basil score doubled (0.5 to 1.0).
open_questions.why_unresolved: The drift rate is a placeholder; there is no carbonate alkalinity balance, no source-water alkalinity and no buffer dosing outside the pH_control flag.
open_questions.evidence_still_needed: Sourced nitrification alkalinity consumption, source-water alkalinity for NL and India sites, and a buffering model; until then validation runs hold pH at the published mean.
open_questions.resolution_note: 2026-11-26 (pH buffer pass): a carbonate alkalinity buffer is in as a candidate (src/ph_buffer.py, model carbonate_alkalinity_buffer in data/knowledge/models/water_chemistry_models.json, opt-in per scenario). Alkalinity is a daily balance (nitrification -7.05 g CaCO3 per g N, Ebeling 2006; optional returns from NH3 excretion, denitrification and plant nitrate uptake; water exchange; base dosing) and pH is solved from alkalinity and a held dissolved CO2. pH-free validation (reported, not scored): with nitrification only, Knaus pH falls from 8.0 to about 5.2-5.5 within 70 days whatever the source water, because alkalinity runs out; with all returns at their upper bounds and tap or hard water it stays at 7.8-7.9, close to the published 8.0. UVI base check: nitrification only needs about 168 g base per kg feed (13 to 15 times UVI's 11-12.5); all returns at upper bounds need 24-27 g/kg (about twice UVI). Scored runs still hold pH (Batch 005, B1) because start alkalinity, source water and exchange are not reported. Remaining question moved to UQ-019 (which alkalinity returns to credit by default).

open_questions.issue: The buffer model only reproduces real systems when alkalinity returns are credited: nitrification alone drains alkalinity in weeks and needs about 15 times UVI's recorded base; all returns at upper bounds still need about twice UVI's base.
open_questions.why_unresolved: No source measures the alkalinity released by plant nitrate uptake in aquaponics, the denitrified share of the UVI residual N loss, or states how fish NH3 excretion should be counted. UVI make-up water alkalinity and how much make-up replaces evapotranspiration are also unknown.
open_questions.evidence_still_needed: A dosed or undosed aquaponics pH and alkalinity time series with feed, exchange and source-water alkalinity (to calibrate the three return terms); Rakocy 2004 Acta Hort 648 full text; EPA nitrogen-control manual for the excretion convention; measured dissolved CO2 in raft aquaponics.
